sections.h2: Where is Lenexa, Kansas, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Lenexa is a Johnson County city on the west side of the Kansas City area. The Census Bureau lists 34.45 square miles, more than double Leawood's footprint.

The Census counted 57,434 residents in 2020, and Wikipedia gives a 2023 estimate of 58,536. Lenexa has no school district of its own, so a street address decides whether a family attends Shawnee Mission, Olathe or De Soto schools. A buyer relocating to the area will ask that early.

sections.h2: What is the history of Lenexa?
sections.html:
Lenexa was platted in 1869 by Octave Chanute, a railroad civil engineer, on land that included 10.5 acres bought from C. A. Bradshaw along a railroad right-of-way. The name comes from Na-Nex-Se, the wife of Shawnee Chief Black Hoof.

The land has an earlier story. In 1857 James Butler Hickok, later known as Wild Bill Hickok, staked a 160-acre claim at what is now 83rd Street and Clare Road, and the Santa Fe Trail ran through the area. The town stayed tiny for most of a century, then exploded. The census counted 5,242 people in 1970, 18,639 in 1980 and 34,034 in 1990.

sections.h2: How much has Lenexa grown, and what does that mean for the houses?
sections.html:
Lenexa grew from 5,242 residents in 1970 to 57,434 in 2020, and the steepest jump came in the 1970s. A large share of its housing was therefore probably built from the 1970s onward, so many houses are now 30 to 50 years old and reaching the age when roofs, HVAC systems, water heaters and windows need replacing.

sections.h2: What employers shape the Lenexa economy?
sections.html:
Lenexa's employer list leans toward logistics, laboratories and engineering. It is the birthplace of Garmin and the regional headquarters of Kiewit Construction, and it hosts a National Archives records center, known informally as the Caves, that stores federal records from agencies in Iowa, Kansas, Missouri and Nebraska.

The city's 2015 annual financial report listed these largest employers. They date from that year, so use them as context only.

sections.h2: What income and education figures describe Lenexa households?
sections.html:
The 2016 to 2020 American Community Survey estimated median household income at $90,487 and median family income at $110,925, and 39.7 percent of residents held a bachelor's degree or higher. About 5.0 percent of the population was below the poverty line.

The city is also home to St. James Academy, its first private high school, which opened in 2005, and a Johnson County Library branch at Lenexa City Center. Johnson County Transit provides local bus service. The nearest intercity train and bus stations are in Kansas City, Missouri.

sections.h2: What are Lenexa's rental license rules, including short-term rentals?
sections.html:
Lenexa requires a rental license before tenants or guests live in a residential rental property, and the rule includes short-term rentals. The licensing period runs January 1 to December 31, and the city mails printed renewal invoices in mid-November.

  • Plan to apply at least 30 business days before renting.
  • Fees start at $75 per property and depend on the type and number of properties you own in Lenexa.
  • The city does an exterior inspection of every residential rental every other year, or more often if warranted.
  • An owner who lives out of state, or an out-of-state entity with no in-state manager, must name an owner's agent who lives in Johnson County, Kansas.
  • A short-term rental is a stay of less than 30 days, may not host parties or events for non-guests, and may be occupied by one person, a related group, or up to four unrelated adults.

If you own a Lenexa rental you want to sell, check the license status and any open exterior violations first. The city handles status questions at permits@lenexa.com or 913-477-7725. A buyer who purchases as-is can take the house with those items open, which a lender-financed buyer usually will not.

sections.h2: How does Johnson County property tax work for Lenexa owners?
sections.html:
Johnson County bills Lenexa real estate tax, with first-half notices going out in mid-November. The first half or the full year is due on or before December 20, and the County Clerk calculates mill levies for each taxing authority.

Johnson County dateEvent
January 1Valuation date
On or before March 1Appraised value notices mailed
March 31Appeal deadline (30 days after mailing)

December 20First half or full payment, and first half payment under protest

The county credits residential owners against the 20-mill school general levy: 8,625 of assessed value is exempt for tax years 2024 and 2025, worth $172.50. Mail payments go to a St. Louis lockbox address, and the county warns not to mail cash. Late payments accrue interest, and not receiving a statement does not remove it.

sections.h2: How is a Lenexa deed recorded?
sections.html:
The Johnson County Register of Deeds, at 111 S. Cherry Street, Suite 1200, in Olathe, records Lenexa deeds. Walk-in hours are Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

The recording fee is $21.00 for the first page and $17.00 for each added page. The office does not accept documents by email or fax, and a document that misses margin or legibility requirements is returned. The deed itself comes from the title company at closing; it is not held by the county or the lender. For a house you inherited, a Transfer on Death deed must be signed, notarized and recorded before it works as a beneficiary designation.

sections.h2: What should I compare when choosing how to sell in Lenexa?
sections.html:
Compare your net proceeds, your timeline and the work each route requires. A listing, a private sale and a cash sale each trade among those three.

  • Listing: wider exposure, but showings, an appraisal and a lender's timetable.
  • Private sale: no agent fee, but you handle disclosures and the contract.
  • Cash sale: an as-is purchase on a schedule you set, often chosen for rentals with license issues, inherited houses or houses needing a new roof or systems.

We buy houses in Lenexa as-is. Request an offer, and you can weigh it against a listing without any obligation.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental license in Lenexa?
faqs.a: Yes, before any tenant or guest lives in the house, including short-term rentals. Fees start at $75 per property, the license runs January 1 to December 31, and the city inspects the exterior every other year.

faqs.q: When are Johnson County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half or full amount is due on or before December 20. Tax bills are mailed around November 15, and valuation notices go out on or before March 1.

faqs.q: Which school district is Lenexa in?
faqs.a: Lenexa has no district of its own. Students attend Shawnee Mission, Olathe or De Soto district schools, depending on the address.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Lenexa property?
faqs.a: At the Johnson County Register of Deeds, 111 S. Cherry Street, Suite 1200, Olathe. The fee is $21 for the first page and $17 for each additional page.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lenexa house with an expired rental license?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases as-is, so an expired license or open exterior violation does not have to be resolved before closing. Contact permits@lenexa.com or 913-477-7725 to learn the license status.
